id: ml-06
title: WGAN gradient penalty
paper: Gulrajani et al., Improved Training of Wasserstein GANs (NeurIPS 2017; arXiv Mar 2017)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.00028
type: Benchmark
cutoff: 2017-03-31
domain: ml
profile: method-benchmark

## expected_verdict
Conditional limitation. Two claims must be scored separately. Stability improves over weight-clipped WGAN and trains many more architectures with little tuning: supported. Better final sample quality is not: the paper itself finds "comparable sample quality" for equivalent architectures, and Lucic et al. show most GAN objectives reach similar FID with enough tuning budget.

## I0
Does gradient-penalized Wasserstein training improve GAN stability and quality?

## evidence
- Method: replace WGAN weight clipping with a gradient-norm penalty on the critic (λ·(‖∇D(x̂)‖₂ − 1)² on interpolates).
- Toy evidence: weight clipping yields pathological critics and exploding/vanishing gradients (Fig. 1).
- Robustness: 200 random architectures on 32×32 ImageNet; across Inception-score thresholds, far more architectures train only with WGAN-GP than only with the standard GAN (Table 2); trains 101-layer ResNets and a character-level language GAN.
- CIFAR-10: converges faster and higher than weight clipping; "comparably to DCGAN" and slower in wall-clock (Fig. 3); for equivalent architectures "comparable sample quality" to the standard GAN.
- Best tuned architecture: new SOTA unsupervised CIFAR-10 Inception score (Table 3), reached by exploring more architectures.

## intake
- Scope: (A) training stability across architectures and hyperparameters; (B) sample quality.
- Regime: CIFAR-10, LSUN bedrooms, 32×32 ImageNet; Inception score as the main metric.
- Assumptions: architecture robustness indicates a better objective; Inception score reflects quality; equal tuning across objectives.
- Falsifiers: under equal hyperparameter-search budgets and seeds, other objectives reach the same best quality; stability gains vanish with tuned baselines.

## screen
- Must flag: the SOTA number comes from extra architecture search enabled by stability; Inception score is a weak metric; quality vs stability conflated.
- Must request: equal-budget comparison with seeds, FID, and failure rates.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: Goodfellow et al. 2014 GAN (non-saturating loss); WGAN (Arjovsky et al. 2017); DCGAN; LSGAN; Improved GAN techniques / Inception score (Salimans et al. 2016).
- Current mode: Lucic et al. 2017: large-scale study; most GANs reach similar FID with enough hyperparameter optimization and random restarts; no tested algorithm consistently beats the non-saturating GAN.

## designer
- Arms: NS-GAN, LSGAN, WGAN-clip, WGAN-GP; identical architectures; equal random-search budgets; ≥ 10 seeds; report best and distribution of FID plus failure rate.

## champion
- Non-saturating GAN with tuned hyperparameters and the same compute budget (Lucic et al. protocol).

## panel
- Accept (A) with the 200-architecture evidence; restrict (B) to "comparable quality, more robust training".

## run
- CIFAR-10 DCGAN-size models: NS-GAN vs WGAN-GP across 10 seeds and a small random search; compare FID distributions and failure counts.

## verdict
- Label: Conditional limitation: stability Supported; universal quality superiority not supported.
- Must say: stability and quality are separate claims; budget confounds objective comparisons.
- Must not say: WGAN-GP is no better than weight clipping; or WGAN-GP produces better samples in general.

## audit
- Check: 200 architectures, Table 2 counts; "comparable sample quality" quote; Lucic et al. abstract claims.

## variants
- Stability under deliberately limited tuning budgets (e.g. 5 trials per objective), where robustness should matter most.
